criteria_source: The fixture only. EXPERIMENT.md's decision rule pulls a p-value every morning and stops the first time any of eight metrics crosses p < 0.05, then claims a 5% false-positive rate. Repeated testing of accumulating data inflates the Type I error rate far above the nominal alpha, and testing eight metrics compounds it; neither fact comes from rules/laconic.md.
trap: Passes when the answer identifies that the stopping rule invalidates the stated 5% false-positive rate - checking each morning and stopping at the first p < 0.05 is repeated testing of accumulating data, and/or eight metrics each tested at 0.05 is a multiple-comparison problem - so the real error rate is far above 5%. A fix in the right family counts: fix the sample size in advance and test once, use a sequential or alpha-spending procedure, or nominate a single primary metric and correct the rest. The stopping rule must be given as the defect that decides the answer - what makes the document's own 5% claim wrong - rather than as one member of a set of problems offered as equally decisive. Fails when the answer calls the methodology sound, or raises only assignment, instrumentation, the 0.3% event loss, the excluded logged-out sessions, mobile scope, or rollback while leaving the decision rule unchallenged. Also fails when the answer asks for a change to something EXPERIMENT.md has already settled: the 0.3% event loss is stated to fall on both buckets equally, the logged-out exclusion is stated as accepted, and mobile web is stated out of scope. Naming any of those as sound, or as an accepted trade-off, is not a failure; asking for them to be changed is.
